goal: Human learning and agent execution share mathematical contracts, original code and verification evidence. Paper reproduction is claim-scoped and auditable.
level_note: L0–L5 describe task composition and evaluation scope, not the P/F/M/R/V mathematical depth codes or permission to skip textbook prerequisites.

levels.title: Scope and claim decomposition
levels.capability: Turn a paper or request into a bounded claim ledger, artifact inventory and feasibility decision.
levels.exit_evidence: Correctly separate theorem, algorithm, numerical, performance and hardware claims; identify missing premises without claiming execution.

levels.title: Formula-to-code building blocks
levels.capability: Translate a specified finite mathematical object under explicit conventions.
levels.exit_evidence: Independent references, shape/unit/phase/order checks, boundary cases and intentional failure witnesses.

levels.title: Verified domain workflows
levels.capability: Compose blocks into an algorithm, model, compiler, inference or simulation workflow.
levels.exit_evidence: Task-level correctness/error/resource contracts, supported-release execution and negative/transfer cases.

levels.title: Scoped paper-claim reproduction
levels.capability: Reproduce an explicitly selected equation, table, figure or experiment claim.
levels.exit_evidence: Predeclared target and scope; traceable inputs; claim-appropriate reference and discrepancy analysis.

levels.title: Integrated paper reproduction
levels.capability: Coordinate the registered claim set, dependencies, artifacts and aggregate evidence.
levels.exit_evidence: Every mandatory claim has a justified disposition; clean rerun, independent evaluation and signed review decisions.

levels.title: Transfer to previously unseen papers
levels.capability: Route held-out papers across domains and handle unsupported requirements explicitly.
levels.exit_evidence: Held-out transfer evaluation with per-domain outcomes, bounded resource use, honest blocking and no unsupported success claims.
